summary.prose: Review each selected task against one explicit final revision while preserving immutable commit provenance and caller-selected scope. Implement bounded projection, identical native/controller inputs, durable reassessment/recovery and offline final-scope history, then qualify complete terminal storage capacity before coordinated rollout. Ten dependency-ordered tasks cover the approved standalone LLD; all 35 test subjects are mapped explicitly, with no adjacent reliability fixes or live deployment included. Task-level test gates exercise each task's own implementation boundary; testStrategyCoverage retains exact LLD subject text and maps collective coverage across the listed tasks. The independently user-authorized test-only repair expectation correction is baseline maintenance, not an added production scope. User clarification2026-11-07: T8's JSON bound is configurable through review.maxJsonBytes (default4194304). Every attempt requalifies retained history; when a budget is full, raising it may admit a fitting attempt without rewriting history. This supersedes only fixed-capacity language; all35 LLD subjects and other task scopes remain.

tasks.title: Pinned input and history contracts
tasks.summary: Construct fresh strict submission schemas requiring reviewRevision and historical optional-pin readers; define proposed projection, decision, binding and snapshot types.
acceptanceChecks: PacketSchema.required includes reviewRevision; reject symbolic/missing/noncommit pins and fresh before-block selections; historical no-pin bytes remain readable.
Use existing typed Git ancestry adapter; preserve source/transport integrity errors and never infer HEAD.
Strict pending/accepted/failed and accepted/unmapped branches require their correct fields.

tests.name: Required-pin PacketSchema/decodeReview rejects absent or symbolic pins and fresh before blocks; historical schemas decode unchanged old packets.
Pinned commit object and ancestry checks reject unavailable, noncommit or nonancestor input and preserve source/transport/integrity errors.
Original parent, changed-hunk and safe-path validation remains strict; caller-supplied projection metadata is rejected.
New pinned zero-segment origins reject scope_conflict before source work, checkpoint replacement or provider dispatch; historical metadata decoding remains unchanged.
Same-attempt resume rejects a changed pin; interrupted no-pin history cannot execute and its checkpoint bytes remain unchanged.
Strict pending/accepted/failed and accepted/unmapped schema branches require their own fields and refuse cross-branch fields.

tasks.title: Exact final interval and blob projection
tasks.summary: Implement serial committed-object projection of original selected intervals, including stable entry indexes, exact shifted spans and deletion boundaries.
acceptanceChecks: Identical blob OIDs map without a changed-text diff; offsets, overlapping partial runs and empty-file anchor zero are exact.
Every nonempty original segment is partitioned into surviving/superseded/deleted dispositions; zero-segment pinned origins reject scope_conflict.
No fuzzy matching, unselected gap coalescing, whole-file empty scope or source mutation.

tests.name: Identity/shifted-line interval mapping preserves selected text and excludes unrelated insertions and worktree canaries.
Changed runs split original intervals into exact surviving and superseded source parts without inventing active historical scope.
Normalize overlapping final intervals with origin accounting, preserve deletion anchors including empty-file zero and never coalesce unselected gaps.
Invalid UTF-8/binary textual mapping and unprovable interval boundaries fail explicitly without dropping origin entries.

tasks.title: Witness lineage and bounded projection
tasks.summary: Verify replacement witnesses, selected renames and merge resolution scope, and enforce source/projection limits.
acceptanceChecks: Replacement witnesses are strictly later ancestor-verified selected origins; reject cycles, unknown indexes and unselected interference.
Actual Git rename chains determine final paths; ambiguous/colliding/unselected paths and merge replacements reject.

10000 reads, 100000 fragments, 64 MiB cumulative decoded source bytes, the existing 4 MiB packet JSON limit and the existing 2 MiB Git diff limit retain approved error-field distinctions; all reads are serial.

tests.name: Selected later ancestor-verified witnesses justify full/partial replacement or deletion; unknown, cyclic or backward witnesses and out-of-set overwrite reject.
Actual selected rename and merge-resolution lineage maps exact final paths; unverified/colliding paths and unselected conflict resolution reject.
Projected entry segments equal normalized active disposition union; fully superseded nonempty origins retain complete dispositions with findingScope=none.
Projection read/byte/fragment bounds and existing input/diff truncation retain their distinct error fields, with serial reads and no preparation/model side effects on refusal.

tasks.title: Effective task scope and route parity
tasks.summary: Thread effective final objects through attribution, native/controller prompts and commands, task schemas and host result validation.
acceptanceChecks: Cover all original changes/tests and replacement-witness closure; preserve none entries as provenance only.
Only final paths/ranges/anchors authorize findings; none never triggers whole-file fallback or previousPath authorization.
Both routes receive equivalent final code, requirements and complete test evidence; coverage mandatory and execution optional.

tests.name: Attribution accounts for all original entries/tests and replacement-witness closure, refusing missing coverage.
The same final blobs/paths/spans reach selectedCode, attributionPrompt, assignmentPrompt, native grants, result schemas and host validation.
Both routes reject historical/unassigned coordinates and all findings on none scopes; genuine final defects and mandatory coverage omissions still block.

tasks.title: Durable attribution decisions and identities
tasks.summary: Persist exact mappings, initial/reassess/reuse decisions, summaries and task bindings; reconstruct without model rediscovery.
acceptanceChecks: Digest binds ordered ids/change indexes/test indexes/decisions/task identities; offline index-only and decision-only tampering reject.
Task identity binds final blob/scope, requirements/docs and full tests, excluding irrelevant global pin movement.
Accepted state saved once before ACK/reuse/dispatch even with no diagnostics; same-attempt conflicts reject.
Reuse requires correct reviewer, prior ordinal and matching inputs; exact durable decisions survive interruption before completed origin exists.

tests.name: Canonical accepted task rows, decisions, task identities and summary persist before ACK/reuse/dispatch even without diagnostics.
Canonical final-attribution-v1 binding detects changed indexes, selectedTaskIds, testCount, state or decisions; shared valid rows and empty scopes remain valid.

Task identities bind final relevant source, requirements/doc identities and full assigned tests; unrelated global pin movement permits reuse while changed relevant inputs or wrong party/source ordinal reject.
After loss of memory restore exact mixed reassess/reuse action/reason/sourceAttempt and summary without attribution rediscovery; no completed origin is fabricated before actual reuse completion.

tasks.title: Checkpoint save outcomes and explicit recovery
tasks.summary: Classify not_replaced/replaced/uncertain failures and fence until source-validated exact reconciliation and successful explicit re-acknowledgement.
acceptanceChecks: Pre-rename and post-rename directory/cleanup failures classify accurately; preserve ignored unsupported sync policy.
Every failed acceptance save prohibits ACK/provider/reuse/task dispatch, no pending rollback overwrite or model-failure relabel.
Exact prior/candidate readback under owner; unreadable/conflicting disk stays fenced.
Explicit resume validates projection/mapping/decisions/hashes then successfully saves same accepted mapping; another failure remains fenced, no automatic storage retry.

tests.name: Pre-rename file open/write/sync/close and rename failures classify not_replaced; post-rename directory/cleanup failures classify replaced; uncertain/read-failed outcomes remain explicit.
Every failed acceptance acknowledgement fences both routes with no dispatch or rollback overwrite and no attribution/model-failure relabel.

Explicit recovery compares exact prior/candidate under ownership, validates source/mapping/bindings and obtains a successful same-mapping save ACK before continuation; repeated failure/conflict remains fenced.

tasks.title: Pinned permanent history and unmapped failures
tasks.summary: Publish source-verified final snapshots; validate, merge and render accepted and unmapped history offline using saved task scopes.
acceptanceChecks: Final renamed/shifted coordinates roundtrip without Git in synchronous readers; original paths cannot authorize findings.
Accepted cannot downgrade; partial pinned snapshots reject; index/decision binding rechecks offline; duplicate publication idempotent and conflicts reject.
Attribution failure publishes actual bounded error, all selected failed/incomplete outcomes, no invented mappings/identities/findings/reuse; next attempt allowed only after publication.
Historical no-pin completed records remain unchanged/read-only; source-aware full task identities checked before publication.

tests.name: Source-verified final snapshot publication and offline merge/validate/render roundtrip preserve shifted/renamed per-task scope, provenance and byte-idempotence without live Git in readers.
Accepted/unmapped snapshot required fields, partitions, witness closure, task subsets and canonical bindings reject tampering, omitted metadata and foreign findings.

Attribution timeout/provider/invalid-scope failure publishes every selected failed/incomplete outcome with true bounded diagnostics, no invented identity/findings/reuse or accepted downgrade, then allows the next sequential attempt.
Completed historical no-pin histories remain byte-identical/read-only and cannot authorize fresh unpinned execution.

tasks.title: Full terminal-envelope capacity gates
tasks.summary: Preflight complete terminal checkpoint/CR envelopes against configurable review.maxJsonBytes, retain full failure/diagnostic capacity, and permit raising the budget without rewriting history.
acceptanceChecks: Before admission save/ACK/provider qualify failed and incomplete envelopes against review.maxJsonBytes (positive safe integer bytes, live configuration, default4MiB), including prior history, tasks, snapshots, diagnostics/repair/completion metadata and escaped pretty JSON.
Store shared failure once with code <=64 and summary <=8192 UTF-8 bytes; preserve 32 KiB diagnostics policy, no trimming/dropping to fit.
Check actual accepted mapping before save and later result/diagnostic growth against remaining terminal reserve; external/storage conflicts explicit.

Reject oversized10000-task small-input units before save/model. Exact-fit admitted units can fail attribution and publish all outcomes. Every next attempt requalifies retained history against the configured limit; refuse explicitly when full, and admit fitting attempts after raising the setting without rewriting history.

tests.name: Actual pretty checkpoint and merged CR serializers qualify failed/incomplete terminal reserves against configurable review.maxJsonBytes (default4MiB), including all tasks, prior history, mapping/decisions, diagnostics and completion metadata before save/ACK/provider.
Exercise 10000-task small-input overflow, exact-fit/one-byte-over, long IDs and escaped/Unicode diagnostics at unchanged 32 KiB aggregate policy with shared bounded failure detail.

Both routes preserve terminal reserve through accepted mapping and later results/diagnostics; boundary failures publish all outcomes, next attempts requalify and can be admitted after raising configured capacity without rewriting history; oversized work dispatches/saves nothing.

tasks.title: Submitters, MCP and coordinated transition
tasks.summary: Update every fresh packet producer, MCP schema and guidance; document operator-controlled transition after full qualification.
acceptanceChecks: Explicit pin required, commit pointers only provenance and supplied change set only scope; missing pin errors actionable.
Drain or explicitly interrupt before coordinated producer/daemon restart; no activation flag, automatic deployment or promised in-flight completion.
Retain upgraded reader after pinned records exist; no blind downgrade or history rewrite; interrupted unpinned work needs new pinned attempt.
Do not implement separate native diagnostics, rejected-result repair or coverage classification issues; sequence/rebase their shared modules.

tests.name: Every fresh in-repo producer and MCP submission schema requires explicit final pin with actionable validation errors and caller-selected change-set scope.

Historical reader and interrupted-unpinned recovery semantics remain route-correct; coordinated producer/daemon rollout documents drain/interruption, no activation flag and state-preserving rollback only.
Adjacent native diagnostics, rejected-result repair and coverage classification ownership remains separate with shared-module sequencing documented.

tasks.title: Semantic regression and production qualification
tasks.summary: Complete all 35 LLD subjects and ac1-ac5 mapping with disposable compiled MCP/IPC smoke and scoped production checks.
acceptanceChecks: Synthetic reproduction uses immutable f0d5da04756e1e96a5043c0063a8891dd2455c7e and 76d3d899a5f144721e2a3328a9933e346be3b600; reviewer result depends on assertions of received final code/test evidence, preserves separate genuine defect, never claims missing checkpoint recovery.
Both routes qualify fresh-memory exact reuse, save fencing/re-ACK, unmapped publication/capacity and isolated review ids/pins/cleanup.
Scoped task-review/MCP tests, TypeScript and production build plus disposable compiled smoke pass; no deployment of partial task commits.
Create explicit commit packet for this implementation only before mandatory independent code review; no generic HEAD scope.

tests.name: Both routes review immutable later-fixed code without stale blocker while retaining a demonstrated final provenance/requiredReferences coverage defect; synthetic reviewer responses assert received final code and test evidence.
Labelled synthetic t3/t9 reproduction uses the two approved immutable commits and durable CR evidence without claiming unavailable raw packet/attribution/timing recovery.
Whole-pipeline fresh-memory reuse, save fencing/re-ACK, final-history publication and capacity tests pass on both routes; independent review ids/pins and cleanup remain isolated.
Disposable compiled MCP/IPC smoke pins final multi-commit scope, excludes unrelated HEAD/worktree changes and publishes truthful final results.
Scoped task-review/MCP tests, production build and complete 35-subject ac1-ac5 traceability qualify coordinated rollout; no partial deployment or direct cloud/retired engine introduced.

testStrategyCoverage.lldStrategyItem: New packets require a full commit reviewRevision; reject missing/symbolic/unavailable/non-commit pins. Same-attempt replay rejects changed pin; historical completed no-pin records remain readable without granting model execution.
Origin selections retain existing parent/hunk/path validation; projected scope is host-derived and cannot be supplied or forged by the caller.

Schema-construction regression: missing reviewRevision is rejected by the actual PacketSchema/decodeReview path, PacketSchema.required includes it, and historical StoredPacketSchema still decodes no-pin records. Cloning/replacing an optional property without rebuilding required must not satisfy this test. [[c2]]
Identity and shifted-line projection preserve only selected surviving text, excluding unrelated insertions and working-tree canaries.

Later selected fixes supersede earlier selected defects: final spans and replacement witnesses are used, original entries remain completely accounted for, and historical-only defect coordinates are not finding scope.
Partial supersession splits selected intervals correctly; overlapping final spans coalesce while preserving every origin index; ambiguous partial replacements fail explicitly.
Selected rename/deletion chains, empty-file line-zero boundaries, wholly superseded entries and deleted files never become unconstrained whole-file scope.

Non-ancestor origins, out-of-set overwrites, conflicting merge resolution, unverified renames, binary/non-UTF8 mappings and truncated/budget-exceeded reads refuse preparation without model calls or dropped scope.
Final-only finding locations and native schema agree; superseded-only entries allow no code findings while genuine final defects still block.
Reuse requires identical final blobs/projected task scope/requirements/test inputs and same reviewer; changed relevant final code forces reassessment while historical feedback remains immutable.

EffectiveTaskChange threading: prove final text reaches selectedCode/assignmentPrompt/native grants, the same final paths/spans reach assignmentResultSchema and validateTaskResult, superseded-only rows reject findings, and ProjectedEntry.segments equals the normalized union of its surviving/deleted dispositions. [[c3]] [[c5]] [[c16]] [[c17]]

Host reuse binding: both routes persist taskScopeIdentities after direct/model attribution even with no diagnostics; sourceAssessment and reuseAssessment reject a changed relevant final blob, scope, requirement or test input and missing identities. Identical task inputs across unrelated revision movement may reuse; conflicting same-attempt identity writes fail. [[c8]] [[c9]] [[c10]]

New pinned zero-segment original selections reject field=scope_conflict before checkpoint replacement or provider dispatch; historical no-pin metadata records remain readable without granting new execution. Nonempty origins that become fully superseded still have complete dispositions and findingScope=none. [[c2]] [[c3]] [[c18]]

Permanent final-scope representation validates required pin/snapshot plus the state-specific accepted/unmapped attribution contract, origin-index partitions, witness closure, per-task subsets and canonical projection identity. Reject omitted, oversized, malformed or tampered pin/path/ranges/task rows/digests and findings in another task’s scope; historical no-pin CR bodies remain readable and byte-identical. [[c10]] [[c11]] [[c12]]

Durable accepted attribution: atomically persist canonical taskId/changeIndexes/testIndexes rows with state=accepted, taskScopeIdentities and attributionIdentity on native/controller/direct paths, even with no diagnostic repair. Reject bad indexes, duplicate tasks/row indexes, omitted changes/tests, missing witness closure and conflicting replacement; unsuccessful save acknowledgement dispatches no task assessment and follows the pre/post-replacement recovery contract. [[c3]] [[c8]] [[c9]] [[c10]]

Offline attribution binding: mutate ONLY one accepted task changeIndexes/testIndexes list (including adding another task’s valid entry) while preserving all existing digest strings. Recomputed final-attribution-v1 identity must reject the record. Test selectedTaskIds/testCount/state mutations, valid shared entries and empty task scopes, and retain full source-aware task-identity verification on resume/publication. [[c10]] [[c11]] [[c12]]

Resource error fields: assert field=input for oversized decoded packet, field=changes for reused truncated Git diff, and field=projection_limit for projection-local read/byte/fragment/snapshot counters. Preserve source/commit/transport-integrity failures; assert no task dispatch and no partially accepted mapping at every budget boundary. [[c2]] [[c3]] [[c4]]

Accepted reassessment persistence: qualify initial/reassess/reuse union rules, durable reason/sourceAttempt and reassessmentSummary, identity binding over decisions, strict absence of sourceAttempt on reassess, and rejection of source-party/ordinal/input mismatch. A planned reuse without a completed origin must remain reconstructible. [[c8]] [[c9]] [[c10]]

Save commit-point qualification: inject temporary open/write/file-sync/file-close and pre-rename failures, rename success followed by directory open/sync/close or cleanup failures, and uncertain/read-failed outcomes. Assert NO acknowledgement/dispatch on every unsuccessful save, correct not_replaced/replaced/uncertain classification, and no rollback overwrite. Exact candidate/prior reconciliation plus explicit successful re-acknowledgement determines recovery; do not assert unchanged pending bytes after successful rename. [[c10]]

Terminal capacity qualification: use real checkpoint/CR serializers and runtime attribution-terminal result constructor for failed/incomplete branches. Exercise the 10000-task small-input case, exact just-fit/one-byte-over limits, long IDs, escaped/Unicode diagnostics at the existing 32 KiB aggregate cap, shared failure detail, preexisting checkpoint/CR history, completion metadata, accepted mapping decisions and remaining-outcome reserve. Reject oversized admission before any provider/save; do not trim tasks or diagnostics to fit. [[c2]] [[c10]] [[c11]] [[c21]] [[c22]] [[c23]]

Whole-story task A introduces a defect and task B fixes it in the same submitted set: native and controller routes review the fixed final version without a stale blocker, while a separate unresolved final defect still blocks. Reproduce the actual S3 t3/t9 pair: the t3 first-report lookup is fixed by included commit 76d3d899a, and the final reviewed source must not retain its historical blocker. [[c1]]
Attribution accounts for every original entry, including superseded entries, and every supplied test; cross-task final source is shared with origin references rather than obsolete embedded versions.
Resume, new attempt, publication and BUILD freshness retain the pinned final revision; completed historical no-pin records stay unchanged and cannot be resumed or reused as final-version execution.

A task assigned a fully or partly superseded origin must also cover its final replacement/deletion witness entries; omission is an attribution error, not a vacuous pass. Unknown/cyclic/backward-incompatible witness references are rejected.

Genuine current test-coverage/provenance defect non-regression: alongside a historical defect fixed later in the packet, deliberately omit a current provenance or requiredReferences test. The final review must still report that demonstrated coverage defect; final-version reconciliation must not suppress it or auto-pass it. [[c1]]

Two independent native/controller reviews with different reviewIds and final pins can progress concurrently; changes, bindings, feedback, optional-execution disclosures and completion/cleanup of one never alter or unblock the other. Provider work remains serial within each review and the existing activity/retry policy is unchanged. [[c1]] [[c13]]

Publish and reread a shifted and renamed final-coordinate finding through publishTaskCheckpoint -> mergeTaskSummary -> validateTaskBody -> renderTaskReview -> validateTaskBody, with source Git access only before publication. Final line 20 remains valid when origin line 10 was selected; old-coordinate and unassigned-task findings reject. A metadata snapshot is saved without blob text; duplicate publication is byte-idempotent and conflicting snapshots reject. [[c3]] [[c5]] [[c11]] [[c12]]

Lose all reviewer memory after accepted attribution in a multi-task review with distinct assigned tests. A fresh publication service loads only the checkpoint and pinned source adapter, reconstructs saved mappings, recomputes task bindings, publishes/renders/rereads the correct final per-task scopes and supports exact resume without a new attribution/model call. [[c3]] [[c8]] [[c9]] [[c10]] [[c11]] [[c12]]

Both native/controller routes: attribution timeout, provider failure, exhausted invalid scope submissions and oversized unaccepted mapping publish an unmapped_failure pinned summary with actual diagnostics, no task identities/findings/reuse and no invented mapping. Verify publication completion and successful next-attempt admission; reject passing results, mapped findings, missing selected terminal outcomes and a false downgrade from accepted state. [[c9]] [[c10]] [[c11]] [[c12]] [[c21]]

Historical reproduction evidence: construct a labelled synthetic explicit packet from durable CR review 1 t3/t9 scope and immutable commits f0d5da04756e1e96a5043c0063a8891dd2455c7e and 76d3d899a5f144721e2a3328a9933e346be3b600. Preserve the separate genuine provenance-coverage defect; make no assertion that the absent temporary packet/attribution/timing was recovered. [[c19]] [[c20]]

Both routes: accept a mixed reassess/reuse plan with distinct test assignments, interrupt before a reuse task executes, discard all reviewer memory, reload and restore EXACT action/reason/sourceAttempt/summary with unchanged hashes and source result. Continue without a new attribution call; copy the exact reused result and create its real origin only after completion. [[c3]] [[c8]] [[c9]] [[c10]]

Both routes: acceptance save visibly replaces pending with accepted mapping but fails its final durability acknowledgement. Assert no task/provider/reuse dispatch and no successful attribution ACK; a fresh explicit resume validates/re-acknowledges that same mapping then restores it exactly. Repeat for pre-replacement pending recovery, another failed acknowledgement and unreadable/conflicting disk state; no automatic storage retry or accepted-plan replacement. [[c8]] [[c9]] [[c10]]

Both routes: a preflight-admitted unit at the terminal capacity boundary times out/fails/exhausts attribution, preserves all selected task outcomes and existing bounded diagnostics, publishes the unmapped snapshot and admits the next sequential attempt. Verify actual bytes for the complete checkpoint and merged CR envelope. An oversized 10000-task unit is refused before provider dispatch; later accepted results/mappings cannot consume the remaining terminal reserve. [[c9]] [[c10]] [[c11]] [[c12]] [[c21]] [[c22]] [[c23]]

Disposable compiled MCP/IPC review packet pins a final revision over a multi-commit story; task review inspects final blocks, preserves origin provenance, excludes unrelated HEAD/worktree changes and publishes the correct current result.
Production build and scoped task-review/MCP tests pass; no direct cloud REST, retired engine or installed-daemon activation is introduced.
